newsitem.title: USA: Ashland asks for meet with Nigeria oil min.
newsitem.headline: Ashland asks for meet with Nigeria oil min.

text.p: Ashland Inc said Tuesday that it had requested a meeting with Nigeria's oil minister after the ministry last week revoked the Kentucky-based company's license to operate in the country.

"Ashland has requested a meeting with the minister of Nigeria's petroleum resources in an effort to clarify issues regarding the company's current business interests in Nigeria," said company spokesman Chuck Rice.
"Ashland will have no further comment until that meeting takes place," he added.

Last Friday, Nigeria's oil ministry said Dan Etete, the petroleum resources minister, had ordered the cancelation of Ashland's production contracts and work permits for its employeess because the U.S. company had transferred its interests to a third party without first getting the ministry's consent.
The Nigerian ministry's statement said Ashland had sold its interests in the Nigerian oil contracts to Perenco Investments S.A., a private French company.
Ashland had not formally heard from the ministry about its action apart from press reports, the company spokesman said.

Ashland's Nigerian interests consist of its offshore ANTAN crude oil floating terminal which collects from six offshore fields (Adanga, Akam, Bogi, Ebughu, Mimbo, Ukpam); it also operates the onshore Izombe field which feeds itno the Brass River terminal.
The overall equity interest is at around 17,000 barrels per day.

As part of its restructuring announced last year, Ashland has sold its U.S. production interests (Blazer Energy) to Norwegian state-owned Statoil, agreed to merge its U.S. downstream with Marathon Oil Co, as well as other moves.
